Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

real adjective

also genuine, a real one

classical

Cic. Off. 2.43: vēra glōria, opposed to ficta
Cic. Verr. 2.4.147: vērus ac germānus Metellus (Lewis & Short)

vērus, vēra, vērum

real, genuine (not fake or pretend)

Opposed to fictus and falsus; the same word as for “true”.

Examples

  • Castella Theodōrus ex tessellīs magnēticīs aedificāre solēbat; castellum vērum numquam vīderat.

    Theo used to build castles out of magnetic tiles; he had never seen a real castle.Libellus I, Iter in Lūsitāniam

  • «Euax! Dracō est! Dracō vērus, tata!» «Dracō marīnus, hippocamporum cōnsanguineus. Vērus.»

    “Wow! It’s a dragon! A real dragon, Dad!” “A sea dragon, a cousin of the sea horses. A real one.”Libellus V, Lisbōna: castellum et ōceanārium

  • vēra glōria rādīcēs agit atque etiam prōpāgātur, ficta omnia celeriter tamquam flōsculī dēcidunt

    real glory puts down roots and even spreads; everything fake drops quickly, like little blossomsCic. Off. 2.43

Other words

  • germānus, germāna, germānum — genuine, real, true to its name

    also used · classical · Cic. Agr. 2.97: illī veterēs germānīque Campānī (Lewis & Short)

    Properly “of the same parents”; in the sense “genuine”, a favourite of Cicero’s (Lewis & Short).

See also true, fact, really?.

SourcesLewis & Short: verus · Lewis & Short: germanus

Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-cicero-philosophica), checked against the editions named there.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 9 November 2026. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word.
